neighbours.label: negation or dismissal word inside a scornful, condemning judgement ('is not worth', 'have no place', 'won't get you anywhere'); neutral, factual negations stay quiet
fire: A promise made by a liar is not worth the paper it is written on.
Cowards who abandon their comrades have no place among honest soldiers.
Blaming everyone else for your failures won't get you anywhere in life.
Such cruelty towards the weak deserves no respect from decent people.
A ruler who robs his own people is not fit to govern them.
Whining about the rules won't earn you anyone's sympathy.
This kind of lazy, dishonest reporting has no value to the public.
Flattery from a hypocrite is not worth a moment of your attention.
quiet: A letter sent by second class post is not likely to arrive before Friday.
The new students have no lessons on Wednesday afternoons.
Taking the earlier train won't change the time we arrive.
The museum does not open before ten on weekdays.
A ruler who serves his people well is fit to govern them.
The recipe needs no sugar because the fruit is sweet.
This kind of careful, honest reporting has great value to the public.
Praise from a trusted friend is worth a moment of your attention.

notes: Card flags the pole broad (1.9% of tokens reach 0.1 of max). Top examples are moralising condemnations peaking on not / won't / no / worth. Probes: 'not worth the bread he eats' 0.62, 'have no place' 0.53, 'won't make the debt disappear' 0.36; 'should not handle money' only 0.10; neutral negations 0.00-0.02.
